recognize_zh: 周邊血中一群大型異常細胞，細胞核有明顯的中央摺痕，呈雙葉或蝴蝶形（bilobed/butterfly nucleus），細胞質少且幾乎看不到顆粒，這是急性前骨髓細胞白血病微顆粒型（APL, hypogranular/microgranular variant）的典型表現。
features: Cluster of large abnormal cells with high N:C ratio in peripheral blood
Nuclei deeply folded with a central groove, producing bilobed, butterfly- or dumbbell-shaped contours
Moderately fine chromatin; nucleoli not prominent
Scant to moderate cytoplasm with few or no visible granules (microgranular); no Auer rods or faggot cells seen in this field
Background normocytic red cells with no platelets conspicuous
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a cluster of large atypical cells with high N:C ratio and characteristic deeply folded, bilobed to butterfly-shaped nuclei with moderately fine chromatin. The cytoplasm is scant and appears largely agranular at light-microscopic resolution, and no Auer rods or faggot cells are identified in this field. Platelets are not conspicuous. Findings are consistent with acute promyelocytic leukemia, microgranular (hypogranular) variant; this is a medical emergency, and urgent coagulation studies, strong MPO confirmation and PML::RARA testing are indicated.

ddx.vs: Monoblasts/promonocytes have folded nuclei too, but abundant grey-blue vacuolated cytoplasm, are MPO weak/negative, nonspecific esterase positive and HLA-DR positive, whereas APL is strongly MPO+ and HLA-DR negative.
Classic APL shows abundant coarse azurophilic granules obscuring the nucleus and frequent faggot cells, while the microgranular variant appears nearly agranular.
Sézary cells have cerebriform grooved nuclei with condensed chromatin and are MPO-negative, CD4+ T cells.
Cup-like blasts have a single nuclear invagination rather than bilobed folding and lack PML::RARA.
